description: Ten years of siege, gods on both sides, then a wooden horse. The greatest epic story of ancient Greece, and the model for every military trick since.

hero.hook: A golden apple, a stolen wife, then ten years of war: Troy does not fall to weapons, it falls to a wooden horse.

blocks.text: The **Trojan War** is the great story of ancient Greece, made immortal by Homer in the Iliad. An alliance of Greek cities besieges [[Ilium]], the other name for Troy, for **ten years**. Gods take sides. Heroes die for honor.
The city does not give in to force. It falls to a trick: the **wooden horse**. That ruse became a universal symbol, from the battlefield all the way to today's computer viruses.

It all starts at the wedding of Peleus and the nymph Thetis. **Eris**, goddess of Discord, is not invited. Furious, she throws in a golden apple engraved “To the fairest.” Three goddesses claim it: **Hera**, **Athena**, and **Aphrodite**.

Zeus asks a mortal to decide: **Paris**, prince of Troy. Hera promises him power, Athena victory in battle, Aphrodite the love of the most beautiful woman alive. He picks Aphrodite. She gives him **Helen**, wife of **Menelaus**, king of Sparta. Paris takes her to Troy. Greece rises to get her back.
At Hisarlik, in Turkey, archaeologists found a city burned around **1184 BC**, a possible site for the historical Troy behind the myth.

**Agamemnon**, brother of Menelaus and king of Mycenae, takes command. A huge fleet sails: Achilles, Ajax, wise old Nestor, and cunning **Odysseus**. The Greeks, or Achaeans, land in the [[Troad]], the region around Troy, and the siege begins.

blocks.caption: The Greek fleet: legend counts a thousand ships

blocks.text: The walls of Troy are said to be indestructible, built with the help of Poseidon and Apollo. For ten years the armies fight on the plain of the [[Scamander]] with no result. On the ground, men die. On Olympus, Hera and Athena help the Greeks, while Aphrodite and Apollo protect the sons of [[Priam]], the old king of Troy.

sections.title: Ten years of siege with no winner

blocks.text: Force is not enough. **Odysseus**, king of Ithaca and master of [[Metis]], the clever kind of cunning, invents the trap. The Greeks burn their camp, pretend to leave, and hide behind the island of [[Tenedos]]. On the beach they leave a huge hollow **wooden horse**, packed with soldiers.

blocks.caption: The Trojan horse: a fake offering with soldiers inside

blocks.text: The Greek spy **Sinon** convinces the Trojans that the horse is a gift for Athena. The priest **Laocoon** shouts that it is a trap and is ignored. Part of the wall is pulled down to bring the horse inside. At night the Greeks climb out, open the gates, and the returning army finishes the city off.
The phrase “the face that launched a thousand ships,” about Helen, comes from the poet Christopher Marlowe. Someone even invented a joke unit of beauty, the “helen,” worth a thousand ships.

Troy burns. Priam is killed. The survivors become slaves. Only prince **Aeneas** escapes, carrying his father and his household gods, the [[Lares]]. Roman legend would later make him the ancestor of Rome. The winners are not spared either: [[The return of the heroes (Nostoi)]] turns tragic for most of them. Agamemnon is murdered. Odysseus wanders for ten more years.

blocks.text: Born from a quarrel among goddesses over a golden apple, the Trojan War ends only after **ten years**, and not by force: the cunning of Odysseus and a wooden horse destroy the city in a single night.
